analysis_md:
# STLA — Stellantis N.V.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-17. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Multinational automaker formed in January 2021 by the FCA–PSA merger: 14 brands (Jeep, Ram, Dodge, Chrysler, Fiat, Peugeot, Citroën, Opel/Vauxhall, Alfa Romeo, Maserati, DS, Lancia, Abarth, Fiat Professional), ~5.5 million vehicles shipped in 2025. Reports in EUR on Form 20-F (IFRS); the NYSE security is the common share itself. Price $4.37 (nasdaq_quote_api); market cap (est) $12.615B — in scope under $40B. Net debt (latest) $18.566B, plus lease liabilities of $2,883.45M in dcf_numbers.json.

## Owner's earnings
Conservative OE = OCF − capex − SBC, from financials_history.csv (USD, FX-converted):
- FY2021: OCF $21,118,459,600; capex $9,838,896,200; OE $11,228,596,400 = $3.56/share
- FY2022: OCF $21,288,269,400; capex $9,188,759,000; OE $12,051,513,400 = $3.81/share
- FY2023: OCF $19,839,170,000; capex $11,263,265,000; OE $8,526,180,000 = $2.72/share
- FY2024: OCF $1,594,711,500; capex $11,490,234,000; OE −$9,942,273,000 = −$3.34/share
- FY2025: OCF −$5,463,750,000; capex $9,384,725,000; OE −$14,901,350,000 = −$5.16/share (latest FY OE total −$14.901B, key_numbers.md)

The maintenance definition (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC) prints the same totals as the conservative definition in financials_history.csv for these years, so the two definitions do not rescue the picture. OE-positive years (last 5): 3/5 (key_numbers.md).

**Base used = normalized 3-yr median OE/share: −$3.34** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; latest FY −$5.16). The base is negative, so the engine emits Tier F (sub-type: no_cash_generation — OCF − capex is not positive) and no DCF, IRR, or IV is supportable. No TTM base: ttm.py reads us-gaap only and exits for this IFRS 20-F filer ("ocf: no annual (FY) fact; sbc: no annual (FY) fact…"), so per the worker spec the median base is used and stated as such. Post-FY evidence (company H1 2026 release, July 30, 2026): H1 2026 net profit €670M and adjusted operating income €1,733M on net revenues of €81,614M, with full-year 2026 guidance of a mid-single-digit revenue increase, a low-single-digit AOI margin, and industrial free cash flow improved year over year (positive IFCF guided for 2027) — a stabilization signal, not a TTM owner's-earnings base, and far below any 15%-hurdle cash generation on this share count.

## OVERRIDES — sbc (filing) and ads_ratio 1.0
- **The gaps:** the preliminary engine run exited with `DATA_GAP:sbc` (sbc missing for fiscal years 2023, 2024, 2025 — sbc_tag is blank for every year in the filed history) and `ADS_RATIO_MISSING` for this 20-F filer. No tier was emitted, correctly.
- **sbc_override (kind "filing", €45,000,000, declared in EUR — the engine FX-converts):** the FY2025 Form 20-F's Share-based Compensation Expense disclosure reports total PSU/RSU award expense of approximately €73M (2025), €45M (2024) and €189M (2023). €45M is the filed FY2024 figure, and FY2024 is the median year of the 3-yr normalized base, so the base is built from the exact filed figure for its year; the single-value fill error on the other years is at most ~€144M/yr against OE totals in the billions and changes no year's sign. It is out-of-band by construction (no filed SBC value exists for the band to anchor on) — the ack_reason is recorded in judgment.json. **Measured impact (key_numbers.md): base OE/share −$3.33 (no override) → −$3.34 (with override), +0.47%; the override is the only reason a tier exists at all (unblocks tier: YES).**
- **ads_ratio {ratio: 1.0}:** the 20-F cover registers "Common Shares, par value €0.01 per share" (trading symbol STLA) on the NYSE — there is no ADS program; the traded security is the common share itself, also listed on Euronext Paris and Milan under the same ISIN. Per-share figures are therefore directly comparable to the $4.37 price with no scaling (flag ADS_RATIO_APPLIED, x1.0).

## Moat: 3/10 — weak
Justification: scale and a few genuine brand franchises are real, but they have not produced durable pricing power, share defense, or through-cycle returns (see ROIC below).
- FOR: scale — one of the world's largest automakers (~5.5M units shipped in 2025), shared platforms and purchasing leverage across 14 brands; Jeep and Ram franchises in North America (47% and 34% of 2025 U.S. sales respectively — the group's historic profit pool); leading regional positions — #2 OEM in EU30 (~16% share in 2025), #1 in EU light commercial vehicles (~28.6%), market leader in South America (~19% share; #1 in Brazil and Argentina).
- AGAINST: share erosion on both sides of the Atlantic (Europe 20.2% in 2021 to ~14-16% in 2025; U.S. 12.0% to 7.7%); no pricing power in the downcycle (2024-2025 revenue pressure from price cuts and high incentives); commodity mass-market product facing Chinese EV entrants in Europe; 14-brand sprawl, and an EV strategy over-investment that forced the ~€25.4B of 2025 reset charges.
- **ROIC evidence (fundamentals.json roic_proxy series):** 15.68% (2019), 16.96% (2020), 34.42% (2021), 32.84% (2022), 27.37% (2023), 3.42% (2024), −29.71% (2025). Gross margin (fundamentals.json): 20.97% / 19.74% / 19.73% / 19.64% / 20.12% over 2019-2023, then 13.08% (2024) and −1.38% (2025). The 2021-2023 returns were shortage-cycle pricing, not a structural moat — they vanished the moment volumes and pricing normalized. A moat above 3 is not supportable on this record.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years (key_numbers.md) — moot here, since no DCF runs on a negative base.

## DCF — none
Tier F by numbers: no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings, so the engine runs no scenario DCF — implied IRR (weighted and base) and IV@15% are null in dcf_numbers.json / score.json, and no hurdle-clearing price is computable. The five-scenario machinery (probs 10/25/30/25/10, default offsets and multipliers, growth blend 13.68% in key_numbers.md) is recorded but unused: the growth blend itself is an artifact of the basis break below and the latest revenue YoY of 10.67%, and quoting scenario outputs on a negative base would be inventing numbers. The growth-start sanity check is therefore moot for the verdict; the operative facts are the sign and size of the OE base (−$3.34/share median, −$5.16 latest) against a $4.37 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing-sourced sbc_override above; data_gap_uncovered is empty in the final run.
- **ADS_RATIO_MISSING** (preliminary run): resolved by the ads_ratio {ratio: 1.0} judgment field above — direct listing, no ADS program; final run carries ADS_RATIO_APPLIED x1.0.
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc**: see OVERRIDES — gap, decision, source, and measured impact (−$3.33 → −$3.34/share) are all recorded in judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json (overrides_applied / override_impact) and key_numbers.md.
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 10 months ago — FY2025 ended 2025-12-31): ttm.py cannot build a TTM base for an IFRS filer (us-gaap only; it exited with no annual facts), so the median base stands per spec. The H1 2026 release quoted under Owner's earnings is the post-FY check: back to a small net profit (€670M) and positive AOI, but guided to only a low-single-digit AOI margin for 2026 — nothing that restores a positive normalized OE base yet.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count −3.01%/yr, key_numbers.md): already credited via the +3.01% growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted. With a negative OE base the shrinking count makes per-share losses smaller over time, not the tier better.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT**: the break is the January 2021 FCA–PSA merger that created Stellantis — revenue steps from $58,478,767,600 (2020, pre-merger basis in the filed history) to $169,231,959,400 (2021). Pre-2021 years are not comparable to the merged group; the 5-yr revenue CAGR of 25.27% and the 13.68% growth blend straddle the break and are not trusted as growth inputs. The 3-yr revenue CAGR is −1.98% and the latest YoY is +10.67% (key_numbers.md) — the post-merger series is the only usable one, and it shows a shrinking, then stabilizing, top line.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): net income −$26,240,100,000 vs OCF −$5,463,750,000 in financials_history.csv. The one-offs are the 2025 strategic reset: ~€25.4B of charges in H2 2025 alone per the FY2025 results release — platform impairments (€6,583M in the full-year fact sheet), product-plan realignments and program cancellations (€9,072M), battery-JV charges (€2,054M), hydrogen fuel-cell discontinuation (€1,094M), a warranty-estimate change (€4,130M), Takata recall (€622M) and restructuring (€913M) — largely non-cash impairments, which is why OCF is far less negative than net income; but OCF is still negative, so the divergence explains the gap without rescuing the base.
- **FX_CONVERTED**: reporting currency is EUR, converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion (2023: 1.105, 2024: 1.0389, 2025: 1.175). All USD figures above inherit that simplification.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the collapse of the cash machine, not the price: OE/share went $3.81 (2022) → $2.72 (2023) → −$3.34 (2024) → −$5.16 (2025) while capex stayed at ~$9-11B/yr. Even excluding every 2025 reset charge, adjusted operating income for FY2025 was a loss (−€842M per the FY2025 fact sheet), so this is not purely an accounting-write-down story — the underlying business lost money in 2025 before the charges.
- Bull case, stated fairly: the price ($4.37, ~$12.6B market cap) already prices deep distress; H1 2026 shows a return to small profits, North America recovering, and management guiding to improvement with positive industrial FCF in 2027. If OE merely returned to the 2023 level ($2.72/share), the stock would clear 15% easily at this price. But that is a turnaround bet on a normalized base that is currently negative — the sweep's Tier F is a statement about the filed base, not a claim the equity is worthless.
- Balance sheet: net debt $18.566B (key_numbers.md) exceeds the $12.615B market cap; the dividend was suspended for 2026 per the FY2025 results. Leverage plus negative OE is the risk pairing, and credit sits one notch above junk per contemporaneous reporting — no position sizing argument survives a second reset year.
- Method range: any defensible method today lands on F for the scored base (median and latest bases are both negative). The range that matters is forward-looking and unscored: 2023-style OE ($2.72/share) would tier high; a repeat of 2024-2025 tiers F at any price. Pass 2 / a future re-score after FY2026 filings is where this name gets re-decided.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (tier_by_numbers F, no tier override) — no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings; F sub-type no_cash_generation.
- Confidence: **Low** (IFRS filer, FX-converted flows, basis break in the history, and a business mid-reset — but the sign of the OE base is not in doubt on any filed year pairing of 2024-2025).
- One-liner: Global auto scale, moat 3/10 — Tier F on this screen: normalized (3-yr median) conservative owner's earnings are negative (−$3.34/share, latest FY −$5.16), so no 15% hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
